result.fixture_scope: Supply-only test was instructed with clip completely absent from adapter and router, free RESET grabber, router own power/cables/battery removed and only resistor-limited VCC/direct ground connected. These conditions were not separately restated in the voltage reply.
findings: Source side remains near nominal 1.8 V under this limited load; Pi boots normally with resistor in place.
The J2507 board supply draws current and settles at only 0.423 V in the supply-only setup, without relying on a seated clip/SPI connection.
0.423 V is below Micron MT25QU256ABA specified 1.7-2.0 V operating supply. No SPI acquisition selected.
limitations: This does not prove either flash chip is defective, a hard short, a particular backfeeding path, TPM cause or the precise mechanism of the earlier connected Pi failure.
The test changed both SPI/clip attachment and supply impedance; it does not by itself isolate all causes of the original direct-clip startup failure.
Neither prior unpowered 540 ohms nor this operating point determines the current required at 1.8 V. Do not extrapolate a fixed board resistance or call 13.8 mA the full-voltage current.
Normal source voltage at this limited load does not establish adapter capability for unrestricted in-circuit acquisition.

With the same approximately 1.8 V source and 99 ohm limit, similar board voltage/loading would be expected. A change of programmer does not remove the shared board load.
The prior Pi source already held 1.793 V at about 13.8 mA; a CH341A supply-only comparison does not by itself qualify unrestricted power or SPI reliability.
Correct earlier implication that a bench supply must be obtained before any further bounded test: existing CH341A may be evaluated first.

resistor_load_comparison.purpose: Compare CH341A versus Pi under the same resistor-limited supply-only board load; exclude the full clip/SPI paths that differed in the 0.568 V trial.
preparation: Unplug CH341A USB and verify adapter OUTPUT 8-to-4 returns to 0 V before changes.
Clip cable remains unplugged from adapter, Pi fully disconnected, router own power/cables/battery removed, cooling off; RESET grabber free.
Restore only adapter OUTPUT 8 -> measured 99 ohm resistor -> blue J2507 pin 8, and adapter OUTPUT 4 -> purple J2507 pin 2. Other adapter output contacts unused.
Use the previously checked series assembly (99.6 ohm complete VCC path, 0.3 ohm ground); no new continuity results claimed. Switch meter to DC volts.
resistor_load_comparison.power_action: Power CH341A once; no flashrom or clip operation.

measurements.A: Resistor source-side leg toward adapter OUTPUT 8
measurements.B: Resistor board-side leg toward blue J2507 pin 8
measurements.reply: A, B in V DC and whether B is steady

resistor_load_comparison.stop_and_finish: If A exceeds 2.0 V, unplug immediately. Otherwise unplug CH341A USB after taking readings. No powered wiring changes or resistor bypass.
resistor_load_comparison.status: Complete: owner reports source leg 1.793 and supply/board leg 0.423; matches prior Pi A/B at reported precision. Subsequent USB unplug and socket mounting confirmed.

result.mode: DC volts per quoted/requested test; numeric reply interpreted in that context.
result.common_reference: J2507 pin 2 / GND, per requested test.
result.endpoint_scope: A is resistor leg toward adapter OUTPUT 8; B is resistor leg toward blue J2507-8, as requested. Owner calls B supply leg in the quoted request context.
result.stability_and_timing: About 10 seconds and stability were requested. Exact elapsed time and steadiness not separately stated in this reply; do not import earlier Pi steady qualifier.
result.calculation: (1.793 - 0.423) V / 99 ohms = approximately 13.8 mA. Prior complete VCC path 99.6 ohms is retained separately; current is inferred, not measured with an ammeter.
result.fixture_scope: Owner quotes the instruction for CH341A -> adapter -> 99 ohm resistor -> J2507 VCC, direct ground, clip cable absent and Pi disconnected. Exact resistor/wire placements not independently photographed.

comparison_with_pi.scope: Displayed/reported values match to supplied precision; not proof of identical startup transients, source capacity or all electrical conditions.

assessment: Changing from Pi supply to CH341A did not change this bounded-current supply-only operating point.
Both measured source-side values are near nominal 1.8 V at this load, while board-side 0.423 V remains below flash 1.7-2.0 V operating range.

Shared adapter, deliberate series impedance and board loading remain common factors. The result does not establish a defective flash/adapter, a specific backfeed path, a hard short or the cause of original Pi startup failure.
Do not extrapolate full-voltage board current from this operating point or prior 540 ohm unpowered reading. No resistor bypass, stronger-drive trial or SPI read selected.
